current_disclosures.summary: The OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax framework has been adopted by the EU and implemented by many countries with effective dates starting in 2024, although some jurisdictions have not yet adopted corresponding legislation. AMD reported that the impact of Pillar Two on its financials was immaterial for 2024 and 2025, and it continues to evaluate the impact of new safe harbors and exemptions, such as those released by the OECD in January 2026.

comparisons.peer_topic: Factors impacting effective tax rate and variability
comparisons.peer_summary: Changes in the volume and mix of profits, business operating models, tax audits, deferred tax valuations, non-deductible expenses, tax credits, tax holidays, tax laws (including OECD Pillar Two), accounting standards, and repatriation decisions can impact the effective tax rate and cash payments. These factors may cause significant variability in financial results.
comparisons.comparison: While AMD specifically concluded that Pillar Two had an immaterial impact on its 2024 financials, Intel (INTC) listed 'global implementation of a minimum tax under Pillar Two' as one of several factors that can impact its future effective tax rate and cause significant variability. Intel's disclosure focuses on the potential for variability and future impacts rather than stating a concluded immaterial impact for the current year, whereas AMD provided a definitive assessment for 2024.

sentences.text: For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Tax Legislation Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD Pillar Two legislation is effective for the company in 2025 and is expected not to materially impact the 2025 effective tax rate. However, other countries including Singapore plan to adopt similar legislation effective in 2026, which would significantly increase tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclosed that enacted OECD Pillar Two legislation was not expected to materially impact their effective tax rates. AMD stated the impact for 2024 was immaterial. Micron (MU) stated that while Pillar Two legislation enacted by EU member states would be effective for MU in 2025, the company did not expect these laws to materially impact its effective tax rate for that period.

sentences.text: For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.

While we do not expect these enacted laws to materially impact our effective tax rate for 2025, additional countries where we operate, including Singapore, have announced plans to adopt Pillar Two legislation.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: While Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in certain jurisdictions starting in fiscal year 2025, it is not expected to materially impact NVIDIA's effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, though new legislation could change this assessment.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA disclosed that the impact of OECD Pillar Two legislation on their fiscal year 2024 financials was immaterial or not expected to be material. AMD explicitly stated the impact for 2024 was immaterial, while NVIDIA noted that although Pillar Two legislation enacted in certain jurisdictions would become effective for its fiscal year 2025, it was not expected to materially impact its effective tax rate or cash flows based on current enacted laws.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD announced a framework for a 15% global minimum tax (Pillar Two), with legislation in certain countries set to apply to the company starting in fiscal year 2025. QCOM does not currently expect a material impact on consolidated financial statements but continues to monitor implementation and OECD guidance.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm (QCOM) reported that the impact of OECD Pillar Two legislation on their financial results was immaterial or not expected to be material. AMD explicitly stated the impact for 2024 was immaterial. Qualcomm stated it does not currently expect a material impact on its consolidated financial statements, although legislation was set to apply beginning in its fiscal year 2025.
